retracted.symptom: web-event hourly profile on 2026-08-04 is not a normal day: hour 05 missing (expected 1.5%, saw 0.0%)
retracted.resolution: hourly aggregates rebuilt against a DST-aware calendar

reason: detector mis-specified: fired on an empty night hour on a non-DST day, which is Poisson noise at ~1 in 2000 per hour-check across ~50k hour-checks. Detector corrected to claim only at European DST boundary days; alert retained.

retracted.resolution: keys versioned by first-seen identity so historical facts keep pointing at the entity they were recorded against

reason: detector mis-specified: the evidence was payment rows re-delivered weeks later with a revised amount_cents but the same order_id, customer_id, paid_ts and processor. That is a restatement in the drop channel, already reported as backfill_restatement, not identifier reuse. Detector now requires the id to point at a different order or customer.

retracted.symptom: feature distribution differs between the early and late periods: PSI(payment_method) = 1.06 comparing the last 45 days with days 120-300 ago, which growth and the annual cycle do not explain (basket value is flat by design)
retracted.resolution: model retrained on a recency-weighted window and monitored per period

reason: detector mis-specified: the categorical divergence was computed over the union of levels, so the arrival of a new payment_method ('bnpl', already reported as new_category_late) drove PSI to 1.09 on its own. Measured over the common support the same comparison gives 0.0003, and channel and shipping_speed give 0.0004 and 0.0002 -- the shared distribution did not move at all. Detector now measures the common support only.

reason: same event as the previous covariate_shift retraction, surviving the first fix. 'bnpl' had by now appeared in both comparison windows, so restricting to the common support no longer excluded it; its growth from 1.4% to 18.4% of orders is the whole of the 0.47. Excluding it, the four original payment methods give PSI 0.002, channel 0.0004 and shipping_speed 0.0001. This is the new-category launch already claimed as new_category_late on 2031-02-07, not an independent distribution shift. Detector now compares only levels that existed before the baseline window opened.
